image.alt: A Philodendron Micans in a white pot, its heart-shaped velvet leaves trailing over the rim in copper and deep green

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, with slower growth

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones, out of direct sun

snap: A trailing Philodendron whose heart-shaped leaves have a soft velvet surface — copper-pink as they open, deepening to near-black green with a faint shimmer. It trails from a shelf or climbs a pole, and is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: A velvet-leaved form of the common heartleaf Philodendron, native to Central America and the Caribbean. Left alone it trails; given a pole or a moss stick it climbs, and the leaves grow noticeably larger when it has something to hold.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top inch of soil has dried. It wilts obviously when thirsty and recovers within hours of a drink, which makes it one of the easier plants to read. Keep it out of direct sun, which flattens the velvet and scorches the thin leaves.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The surface is genuinely velvet rather than glossy, so it catches the light differently as you walk past it. New leaves open copper-pink and darken as they age, which means a healthy plant is showing three or four colours at once.
